nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: IPAFFS-specific client-side JS module that turns the plain file input into a drag-and-drop dropzone (progressive enhancement). The markup itself uses only govuk-* classes; the enhancement is driven by the data-module="dropzone" hook, not a Design System feature.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Not part of the GOV.UK Design System. The Design System file upload is a plain input with no drag-and-drop. The rebuild does not need to replicate the dropzone; the standard govuk File upload (or the newer JS-enhanced multiple-file variant) covers the requirement. Only reproduce drag-and-drop if it is a deliberate UX requirement.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: GOV.UK File upload component (govuk-file-upload) — used as-is without the custom dropzone module.

fields.name: fileUpload
fields.label: Select a document
fields.hint: The document must be: smaller than 10MB; a DOC, JPEG, PDF, PNG or XLS file
fields.requiredEvidence: Mandatory to submit this upload step in the authorised legacy handler: validateAccompanyingDocument delegates to validate, which returns FILE_NOT_SELECTED whenever payload.filename is empty (ipaffs-frontend-upload/service/src/validation/file_upload_validation.js:29-31,73-90). The absence of an HTML required attribute is therefore only a client-markup detail; server-side page validation requires a selected file. This is legacy journey mandatoriness 'as the old system had it' and the rebuild may choose equivalent client-side enhancement.
fields.conditionalOn: The user chooses to add an attachment from either the Latest Health Certificate page or the Accompanying Documents page.
fields.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 action 45 (input type=file id=fileUpload name=fileUpload class=govuk-file-upload; required attribute absent); page-objects/notification/DocumentUploadPage.ts:22-24 (the page object exposes input[type="file"]); workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:339-350 and workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:356-363 (the page is reached from health-certificate attachment upload, while the accompanying-documents path is separately configurable); tests/document/document-upload-valid-health-certificate.spec.ts:26-36 and tests/document/document-upload-valid-commercial-invoice.spec.ts:43-53 (CHED-P accepts JPG, PNG, DOC, DOCX, XLS and PDF uploads)

openQuestions: Evidence pointer for the error-state trace 9a0dedd668a877c909f76fa5c6cac6d56a34412e was WRONG: action 30 is a click on the 'Commodity' task-list link, not the document upload page. The document-upload validation error actually renders at action 45 (Expect toContainText on getByRole('alert')), after action 43 (Set input files, the large invalid file) and action 44 (Click Continue). All error-state evidence cited above uses action 45.

The file input has no `required` HTML attribute and the empty-submit error was not observed in a trace. The authorised legacy validator nevertheless confirms server-side mandatoriness and the exact empty-submit copy is "Select a file" (ipaffs-frontend-upload/service/src/utils/validation_constants.js:3-5; service/src/validation/file_upload_validation.js:73-90). Confirm whether the rebuild should retain that copy or align it with the rendered label "Select a document".

The rendered body copy says DOC, JPEG, PDF, PNG or XLS, but CHED-P upload tests explicitly accept DOCX as well (tests/document/document-upload-valid-health-certificate.spec.ts:6-6,26-36 and tests/document/document-upload-valid-commercial-invoice.spec.ts:8-8,43-53). The authorised legacy constants confirm that docx and xlsx are accepted while the displayed list omits them (ipaffs-frontend-upload/service/src/utils/validation_constants.js:19-23). Confirm whether the copy should name DOCX and XLSX explicitly.

The authorised legacy minimum-size error says "larger than 1KB", but the single-file validator actually rejects only content smaller than TWO_HUNDRED_B (200 bytes) (ipaffs-frontend-upload/service/src/utils/validation_constants.js:7,14-17; service/src/validation/file_upload_validation.js:101-108). Confirm the intended rebuild threshold and copy.

This page uses a custom data-module="dropzone" drag-and-drop enhancement on top of the standard govuk file input. Confirm whether drag-and-drop is a genuine UX requirement or can be dropped in the rebuild.

The govuk-hint element carrying the notification reference ('DRAFT.GB.2026.1525975 - CHEDP') sits OUTSIDE the main content region (page chrome), so it is treated as chrome and not captured as a page field.
